simulation.draws_status: declared fallback; no count in the frozen ladder met every convergence tolerance (ADR-074)
simulation.replacement_rule_description: the best player nobody rosters, after the starting slots and teams x bench bench places are filled, the bench by surplus over the starting-slot baseline

behavior.signal_semantics: add and drop COUNTS over the requested lookback window; never an ADP, never a rank, never differenced against one. Each feed is a top-100 list: a side the feed did not carry is unknown, never zero.

signals.sportsbook_context_statement: The spread, total and implied points are sportsbook numbers read from nflverse's schedule. The draft and rest-of-season models never read them: they move no draft or rest-of-season projection, VORP, rank, tier or Pick of the Week selection. The weekly start/sit projection does read them, for the one game it projects (ADR-096).
signals.expected_points_statement: No expected-fantasy-points reading is published. ffopportunity's expected points are licensed CC-BY-SA 4.0, and whether this site may publish a per-player figure derived from them is an open decision (ADR-086). The rest-of-season model reads them as an input; the card does not print them.

correlation.method: spearman of PIT values -> 2 sin(pi r / 6)

_rule.definition: Among QB/RB/WR/TE players the official report designated for a regular-season game, the share who then appeared in it (a stats row or an offensive snap).

weekly.statement: Next-game fantasy points given that he plays, from weekly-startsit-v1: his role, form and track record through the cutoff, his offence, the opposing defence's allowed points, and the game's sportsbook total and spread. It reads no injury report; the league's report is printed beside it instead. No draft or rest-of-season number reads this model.

explanation.reference: His typical week: everything about him held at this week's values, in ordinary games for him: his team's mean posted lines over its completed games (shrunk toward the league by three games), half at home, his team's indoor share, equal rest and a league-average defence at this cutoff.
explanation.statement: Each term is how far this model's number moved with that input, the others held (exact Shapley values over the game inputs). A model attribution, not a measured causal effect. Weather and injuries are printed as context; weekly-startsit-v1 reads neither, so they carry no points.

reasons.not_in_ngs_summary: Next Gen Stats publishes no season summary for him (it qualifies players by volume).
reasons.ngs_volume_mismatch: His Next Gen Stats season summary does not match his official volume through the cutoff, so it is not used.
reasons.no_combine_forty: No linked NFL Scouting Combine 40-yard dash on file for him.

skill_tree.statement: Descriptive context only: observed regular-season statistics through the board's cutoff, each ranked only against qualified players at the same position. No model, ranking, pick or trade reads it, and nothing is combined into a score.

rule.change_unit: percentage points: current minus baseline, never relative growth
rule.baseline_rule: the retained capture whose age before the latest capture is inside the window and nearest the target (earlier on a tie); never interpolated, backfilled or carried forward
rule.started_change: not published: ESPN states neither percentStarted's denominator nor the week it counts, and lineup-setting cadence would read as a trend
rule.absence_is_not_zero: a player ESPN published no ownership for has no reading, never 0%

espn_ownership.attribution: Rostered % and started %: ESPN Fantasy Football (fantasy.espn.com), read once a day from ESPN's public player data.
espn_ownership.population_statement: ESPN's percentages describe ESPN leagues, not yours: whether a player is free in your league is a separate question. Popularity is crowd interest, not a projection.
espn_ownership.start_context_statement: Started % is ESPN's figure, read while ESPN reported scoring period 9 as current. ESPN does not say which week's lineups it counts or how it is calculated, so no start change or started-among-rostered ratio is shown.

definitions.window: The last N completed regular-season weeks ending at the cutoff, the same calendar weeks for every player. A bye or a missed game is fewer games, never an older week.
definitions.recent_rank: Rank by total points in the window among every player at the position who appeared in it, whichever board lists him. Ties share a rank. No appearance, no rank.
definitions.recent_vs_season: Season rank minus recent rank, in places. Positive means the recent rank is better.
definitions.breakout: A descriptive, heuristic category from fixed thresholds over published weekly ranks and role shares. Not a prediction, not a probability, and read by no model.
definitions.takeover: Three consecutive appearances inside the window, each a top-band weekly finish, with a substantial or clearly increased role over those games.
definitions.sneaking: His two most recent appearances inside the window are top-band weekly finishes with a confirmed role; the three-game condition is not met.
definitions.eyebrow: A one-game watch: his latest appearance is a top-band weekly finish, and earlier games do not establish a sustained pattern.
definitions.insufficient: The sample, the pre-window baseline or the role facts the rule needs do not exist, so no category is stated — not a 'no'.

opportunity_opening.reason: no player met this family's rule in this build

streak_watch.reason: no player met this family's rule in this build

role_battle.reason: every qualifying player already leads a story in a higher-priority family

definitions.window: The last three completed regular-season weeks ending at the cutoff, the same calendar weeks for every player (recent form's Last 3). The baseline is every earlier week.
definitions.appearance: A week with a stats row or an offensive snap. A bye (B) and a game his team played without him (D) are not games and are never zeros.
definitions.opportunity: Targets for a receiver or tight end; carries plus targets for a running back. A team share pools his total over his team's total in the games he played.
definitions.ceiling: P90 of the weekly start/sit model's distribution of his points given that he plays: one week in ten at or above it. Not a 90% chance of a big game, and not a ranking of boom probabilities.
definitions.typical_week: The weekly model's own account of the same player in a typical week (his team's average lines, half at home, equal rest, a league-average defense). The difference is the matchup's modelled effect, counted once.
definitions.espn_rostered: ESPN's public share of ESPN leagues rostering him. It describes ESPN leagues, not yours; an unknown reading is not 0%.
definitions.pace: Points per game × 17: arithmetic extrapolation, not a projection.
definitions.snap_share: His share of his team's offensive snaps. Teammates share the field, so snap shares overlap and never add to 100%.
definitions.red_zone: Carries and targets on plays snapped at the opponent's 20 or closer (inside the five: the 5 or closer), counted from nflverse play-by-play.

limitations: Stories describe completed weeks and the published weekly distribution; none is a forecast of a result, and none says a player is due.
No expected-points estimate is published (ADR-086), so a gap between workload and scoring is described, never quantified as luck.
Snaps are not routes and a target is not a first read: no route, route-tree or coverage claim is made.
ESPN roster share describes ESPN leagues; a low share does not mean a player is available in your league.
League size changes nothing here: no story reads a replacement level or a VORP.

unsupported.claim: Route participation, targets per route run, first-read share, route-tree fit
unsupported.reason: No current-season route or participation source is available (the participation feed refuses 2026; ADR-107).

unsupported.claim: Expected fantasy points, xFP share, points over expected
unsupported.reason: ffopportunity is a model input whose per-player publication is undecided (ADR-086, ADR-091).

unsupported.claim: Situational snaps (third down, two-minute, short yardage)
unsupported.reason: Snap counts are per game; no participation data places a player on a given play.
Not measurable from the available data; average depth of target is not a route tree.
The in-season build loads the current season only; no comparable historical cohort is published.
Archived pregame projections are not retained per week, so a current number is never presented as a past expectation.

definitions.appearance: A game played is a regular-season week with a weekly stats row or at least one offensive snap. Byes and weeks he did not appear are not games.
definitions.points: Total fantasy points scored in weeks 1 through the cutoff, in the selected scoring preset, from the same scoring engine as every projection on the site.
definitions.points_per_game: Total points divided by games played. Blank for a player with no appearances.
definitions.season_rank: Rank by total points among every player at the position who has appeared this season, whatever board publishes him. Ties share a rank (1, 2, 2, 4). The same in every league size; it can change with the scoring preset.
definitions.comparison: Season rank measures points already scored. Rest-of-season rank orders the model's value from here on. Different scoring pace, expected remaining appearances and the model's wider football history can make the two orderings differ; the gap is not a change over time and is not by itself evidence of a model error.
definitions.model_difference: The rest-of-season model counts appearances by weekly stats rows only. A week with snaps and no statistic counts as a game here and not in the model's own inputs.

disclosures.long_absence_definition: has played at least once this season and has not appeared for 3 or more consecutive weeks ending at the cutoff
disclosures.long_absence_statement: This estimate uses no injury or practice-report information of any kind. The model infers absence from appearances alone, so a player cleared to return this week and a player out for the season are identical rows that have not appeared for N weeks. "Has not appeared for N weeks" is what is known; it is not a status or a designation.
disclosures.long_absence_ordering_weakness: Ranking quality inside this group is weak. Measured on 18,951 development rows, the rest-of-season ordering within the long-absence cohort reaches a Spearman correlation of 0.311 against 0.797 on the full universe, so the order of these players relative to each other carries little information.
disclosures.tier_boundary_statement: Rest-of-season tiers are bands, not lines. Membership is highly reproducible (bootstrap ARI 0.857) and tiers order realised remaining value across every adjacent pair, but the exact boundary position is not reproducible (agreement 0.167 against a 0.500 bar), so a player near an edge should be read as belonging to both neighbouring bands.

limitations: Overconfident on high-draft-capital rookies: interval coverage 0.763 against an attainable 0.898, the tightest clause in the promotion gate.
Close to unable to order players returning from a long absence: Spearman 0.311 against 0.797 on the full universe.
Conservative intervals on players with no remaining games: 14.5 wide against a climatological 4.5.
The sealed 2025 evaluation season is spent; any change to the model's outputs would need a fresh one.
Tier boundaries failed the frozen stability gate: a tier is a band, not a line.
There is no injury feature, and the cohort that needs one is measurably the worst.
The simulation draw count is a declared fallback: no count in the frozen ladder met every convergence tolerance.
